title: In EditorInspectorPlugin add_property_editor called from inside of _parse_begin doesn't fetch property lable and tooltip.
body: ### Tested versions 4.5 ### System information Godot v4.5.stable - Windows 11 (build 22621) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) HD Graphics 520 (Intel Corporation; 31.0.101.2115) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-6200U CPU @ 2.30GHz (4 threads) - 15.89 GiB memory ### Issue description I wanted to add custom PropertyEditor via plugin. But when I adding it, it behave strange. First of all - it fetches property right (the property editable by new controll), but it doesn't auto-fetch its name and tooltip if added from `_parse_begin()` or `_parse_end()`. If added from `_parse_category()` it fetches the name (#93616) but lose the tooltip, wich actually important for plugin-development (and it's not only build-in documentation, [user's documentation comments](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_documentation_comments.html) allso not fetched as tooltips in this case). Also Resources, for exemple, doesn't have any categories in Inspector. Only adding from `_parse_property()` with a little workaround fetches both name and tooltip automatically right. There is main script of test plugin to check it: ``` extends EditorInspectorPlugin ## Adds a text custom editor to the begining of exported properties for ## every [Label]. var StringEditor := preload("res://addons/testplugin/inspector_plugin/string_property_editor.gd") var last_object_handled: Label func _can_handle(object): return object is Label func _parse_begin(object: Object) -> void: print(object, " _parse_begin") add_property_editor("text", StringEditor.new(), false) add_property_editor("text", StringEditor.new(), false, "Added from _parse_begin: no name and no tooltip!") func _parse_property(object: Object, type: Variant.Type, name: String, hint_type: PropertyHint, hint_string: String, usage_flags: int, wide: bool) -> bool: if not is_same(last_object_handled, object): print(object, " _parse_property") last_object_handled = object add_property_editor("text", StringEditor.new(), false) add_property_editor("text", StringEditor.new(), false, "Added from _parse_property and have tooltip.") return false #name == "text" func _parse_category(object: Object, category: String) -> void: if category == "Label": print(object, " _parse_category") add_property_editor("text", StringEditor.new(), false) add_property_editor("text", StringEditor.new(), false, "Added from _parse_category: have name but no tooltip.") func _parse_end(object: Object) -> void: add_property_editor("text", StringEditor.new(), false) add_property_editor("text", StringEditor.new(), false, "Added from _parse_end: no name and no tooltip.") last_object_handled = null print(object, " _parse_end") ``` Here's how it looks: And I even can't copy documentation description as `.tooltip_text` - it won't be parsed as documentation format not to mention that it won't have even line breaks. I think that it may be becouse property wasn't parsed and system doesn't get innitial info yet. If we look into our print output we would see such order of execution: ### Steps to reproduce Make a custom PropertyEditor and add it for any Node or Resource and try to fetch any property. Or open my minimal reproduction project and enable TestPlugin. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [inspector-plugin-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23189790/inspector-plugin-bug.zip)
